claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl bond coat is thermally sprayed from 15–45 μm feedstock.
The as-sprayed FeCoNiCrAl coating has a thickness shortfall relative to design requirements.
Post-spray annealing in a low-oxygen atmosphere will induce elemental interdiffusion in the bond coat.
Post-spray annealing in a low-oxygen atmosphere will produce a limited oxide scale on the bond coat.
The oxide formed during annealing is likely to be α-Al2O3.
The limited oxide scale will be dense, stable, and protective.
Interdiffusion combined with oxide formation will cause volumetric expansion of the coating.
The annealing-induced interdiffusion and oxidation will produce a net increase in coating thickness.
Annealing at approximately 800 °C for approximately one hour is a suitable treatment for obtaining the proposed thickness increase.
Using high-purity argon or a reducing atmosphere will minimize uncontrolled oxidation during annealing.
The annealed coating will retain a coherent microstructure.
The annealing-induced thickness increase will occur without compromising coating adhesion.
The post-annealed coating will meet bond-coat requirements for thermal barrier coating systems.
The treatment will remain effective under operating conditions typical of bond coats in thermal barrier systems.
Excessive annealing can cause over-oxidation, deleterious phase transformations, or substrate degradation.
Insufficient annealing may fail to produce enough interdiffusion and oxide-related expansion to increase thickness.

contradictions.description: The material description identifies 15–45 μm as the feedstock particle-size range, whereas the predicted outcome describes the baseline coating itself as 15–45 μm thick, conflating feedstock size with coating thickness.
